raw_discharge_summary: FICTIONAL TRAINING CASE GOLD-001. Adult, age group 50-59, female, English. Admitted 2026-11-10 with community-acquired pneumonia; discharged 2026-11-14. Med-A 500 mg by mouth twice daily for 5 days; take after food. Respiratory clinic review in 7 days. Repeat chest X-ray in 4 weeks. Walk indoors as tolerated. Avoid strenuous activity until reviewed. Severe breathlessness or chest pain: seek emergency care. Fever or worsening cough: contact the treating clinic.

FICTIONAL TRAINING CASE GOLD-002. Adult, age group 60-69, male, English. Admitted 2026-11-08 with acute exacerbation of COPD; discharged 2026-11-13. Med-B 1 tablet by inhalation twice daily for 14 days; rinse mouth after each use. Pulmonology clinic in 10 days. Continue the breathing technique demonstrated by the respiratory therapist, 3 sessions daily, approximately 5 minutes per session. Use the walking plan only as tolerated. Severe breathlessness at rest or blue lips: seek emergency care. Increased sputum or fever: contact the clinic.

FICTIONAL TRAINING CASE GOLD-003. Adult, age group 20-29, female, English. Admitted 2026-11-12 with acute appendicitis; laparoscopic appendectomy performed 2026-11-13; discharged 2026-11-15. Med-C 250 mg orally three times daily for 3 days. Surgical wound review on 2026-11-22. Keep the dressing clean and dry; short walks are permitted. Do not lift heavy objects until the surgical review. Increasing wound redness, wound discharge, or temperature above 38.0 C: contact the surgical team. Fainting or severe abdominal pain: seek emergency care.

FICTIONAL TRAINING CASE GOLD-004. Adult, age group 40-49, male, English. Admitted 2026-11-09 with cellulitis of lower leg; discharged 2026-11-14. Med-D 300 mg orally once daily for 6 days. Clinic review in 5 days. Wound swab result expected in 2 days. Elevate the affected leg while resting. Avoid prolonged standing until reviewed. Rapidly spreading redness or chills: contact the clinic promptly. Confusion or collapse: seek emergency care.

FICTIONAL TRAINING CASE GOLD-005. Adult, age group 30-39, female, English. Admitted 2026-11-11 with acute pyelonephritis; discharged 2026-11-16. Med-E 200 mg orally twice daily; duration not stated. Primary care review after 1 week. Urine culture result expected tomorrow. Maintain the fluid intake discussed with the treating team. Persistent vomiting or worsening flank pain: contact the clinic. Fainting: seek emergency care.

FICTIONAL TRAINING CASE GOLD-006. Adult, age group 70-79, female, English. Admitted 2026-11-06 with heart failure exacerbation; discharged 2026-11-12. Med-F 10 mg orally every morning; duration not stated. Cardiology review on 2026-11-19. Blood test (electrolytes) before the cardiology appointment; exact date not stated. Record weight each morning and bring the record to the clinic. Follow the fluid limit documented by the treating team; numeric limit not included in this note. New or worsening breathlessness or chest pain: seek emergency care. Increasing ankle swelling: contact the clinic.

FICTIONAL TRAINING CASE GOLD-007. Adult, age group 50-59, male, English. Admitted 2026-11-13 with transient ischaemic attack; discharged 2026-11-15. Med-G 75 mg orally once daily; duration not stated. Neurology clinic in 14 days. Outpatient vascular imaging; date not stated. Attend the scheduled neurology review. New facial droop, new arm weakness, or difficulty speaking: seek emergency care immediately.

FICTIONAL TRAINING CASE GOLD-008. Adult, age group 30-39, female, English. Admitted 2026-11-10 with dehydration and gastroenteritis; discharged 2026-11-12. Med-H 5 mg orally as needed for nausea; maximum frequency and duration are not stated. Review with primary care if symptoms have not settled within 3 days. Follow the oral rehydration instructions provided by the treating team; exact volume and schedule are not included. Inability to keep fluids down or reduced urine output: contact the clinic. Collapse: seek emergency care.
